title: Pumpkin seeds vs. sunflower seeds

seo.title: Pumpkin vs. sunflower seeds: nutrition comparison
seo.meta_description: Per 1 oz-ish 30 g: pumpkin seeds provide ~9 g protein and 165 mg magnesium; sunflower seeds ~5.8 g protein, 3.3 g fiber and 7.8 mg vitamin E.
seo.search_intent: Compare pumpkin and sunflower seeds for protein, fiber, minerals and calories

excerpt: Using roasted unsalted references and a 30 g serving, pumpkin seeds provide about 172 calories, 9.0 g protein, 2.0 g fiber and 165 mg magnesium; sunflower seeds provide about 175 calories, 5.8 g protein, 3.3 g fiber and roughly 7.8 mg vitamin E. Pumpkin seeds lead in protein, magnesium and zinc; sunflower seeds lead in fiber and vitamin E.
content_html:
Pumpkin and sunflower seeds deliver almost the same calories in a small handful, but their nutrient strengths are quite different. To keep preparation from distorting the result, both references below are roasted and unsalted.

Per 30 gPumpkinSunflower
Calories~172~175
Protein~9.0 g~5.8 g
Fat~14.7 g~14.9 g
Fiber~2.0 g~3.3 g
Magnesium~165 mg~39 mg
Zinc~2.3 mg~1.6 mg

Calories and total fat are essentially tied. Protein and micronutrients create the meaningful differences.

Pumpkin seeds: protein and magnesium

The USDA roasted unsalted reference provides about 29.8 g protein and 550 mg magnesium per 100 g. Sunflower seeds provide 19.3 g protein and 129 mg magnesium.

At 30 g, that is roughly 9.0 versus 5.8 g protein and 165 versus 39 mg magnesium.

Sunflower seeds: fiber and vitamin E

Sunflower seeds provide about 11.1 g fiber/100 g versus 6.5 g in the roasted pumpkin reference. They are also particularly rich in alpha-tocopherol: about 26.1 mg vitamin E/100 g, or roughly 7.8 mg per 30 g.

Salt can matter more than the seed

Salted versions can contain hundreds of milligrams more sodium per 100 g than unsalted versions. Compare like with like if sodium matters.

Which is better?

Pumpkin seeds have a clear advantage for protein, magnesium and zinc. Sunflower seeds stand out for vitamin E and provide more fiber.

Because their calorie totals are so similar, mixing them is an easy way to combine strengths.

faq.question: Which has more protein, pumpkin or sunflower seeds?
faq.answer: Pumpkin seeds: about 29.8 g/100 g versus 19.3 g/100 g in the roasted unsalted references.

faq.question: Which has more magnesium?
faq.answer: Pumpkin seeds by a wide margin: about 550 mg/100 g versus 129 mg.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Sunflower seeds: about 11.1 g/100 g versus 6.5 g in roasted pumpkin seeds.

faq.question: Are they high in calories?
faq.answer: Both are energy-dense, at roughly 172–175 calories per 30 g in these references.
